impact_description: Diversion of classified government forest land for basalt quarrying requiring MoEFCC Stage-I and Stage-II forest clearance.
evidence_text: Gat No. 82 Part, Village Gargaon, Palghar Taluka. Total lease area: 17.08 Ha, designated as Government Forest Land. Stage-I Forest Clearance application submitted.
notes: Directly documented statutory forest diversion area. Mandatory compensatory afforestation and net present value (NPV) required under Forest Conservation Act 1980.

impact_description: Diversion of classified government forest land for captive basalt quarrying requiring MoEFCC Stage-I and Stage-II forest clearance.
evidence_text: Gat No. 9 Part, Village Khanivade, Palghar Taluka. Total lease area: 15.39 Ha, designated as Government Forest Land. Stage-I Forest Clearance application submitted.
notes: Directly documented statutory forest diversion area. Mandatory compensatory afforestation and NPV required under Forest Conservation Act 1980.

impact_description: Deep hole blasting generates ground vibration and air overpressure impacting nearby rural dwellings. Controlled blasting with electronic delay detonators mandated.
document_page: Gargaon Exec Summary p14; EIA p187
evidence_text: Controlled blasting techniques with non-electric (NONEL) detonators to ensure Peak Particle Velocity (PPV) remains within DGMS permissible limits for village structures.
notes: Qualitative mitigation standard documented. Numerical baseline depends on distance to nearest village structures (1.2 km for Gargaon).

impact_description: Drilling, blasting, secondary crushing, and loading generate airborne PM10 and PM2.5 dust affecting ambient air quality along transport corridors.
document_page: EIA p574 Table 162; Gargaon Summary p13
evidence_text: Fugitive emission control requires wet drilling, dry fog dust suppression at crushers, water sprinklers along haul routes, and 7.5m greenbelt along lease boundary.
notes: Qualitative environmental factor. Numerical scores are avoided as per project constraints.

impact_description: Trailing Suction Hopper Dredgers extract seabed sand over 102.77 sq.km, removing top sediment layer and causing temporary loss of benthic macrofauna.
evidence_text: Total statutory reservation area: 10,277.10 Ha offshore of Daman. Seabed dredging removes benthic infauna (polychaetes, bivalves) within extraction trenches.
notes: Total seabed footprint directly documented in official Gazette notification.

impact_description: Hopper overflow during trailing suction dredging increases suspended sediment concentration (SSC), reducing light penetration and affecting phytoplankton.
document_page: EIA p420 Section 4.8; DPR p332 Section 13.2
evidence_text: Hydrodynamic and sediment dispersion studies model sediment plume dispersal with flood and ebb currents. Dredgers must maintain controlled overflow to minimize turbidity.
notes: Qualitative environmental factor supported by CWPRS plume dispersion modeling.

impact_description: Capital dredging deepens access channel and basin to -20m CD; 6.9 - 7.0 million m3 of suitable dredged sand/silt is reused for Phase 1 reclamation fill.
document_page: DPR p71 Section 2.3.2, p214 Section 8.3; Package 2B p4
evidence_text: Capital dredging volume suitable for reclamation fill estimated at 6.9 to 7.0 million m3 in Phase 1, avoiding offshore dumping and reducing external borrow demand.
notes: Dual environmental aspect: seabed disturbance mitigated by circular economy beneficial reuse of dredged sediment.

impact_description: Permanent transformation of subtidal and intertidal marine area into elevated port land platform protected by breakwater and rock revetments.
document_page: DPR p68 Section 2.2; EIA p30 Section 1.5
evidence_text: Total offshore reclamation of 1,207 Ha (Phase 1: 850 Ha, Phase 2: 357 Ha) created in offshore waters of Vadhavan coast.
notes: Directly documented physical footprint. Zero land acquisition of fertile onshore agricultural or forest land.

impact_description: Movement of 32.1 million tonnes of rock from Palghar quarries by 20-30 tonne multi-axle tippers generates CO2, NOx, and diesel particulate matter along haul routes.
document_page: EIA p575 Table 163; Road DPR p22
evidence_text: Road transport air quality mitigation requires paved corridor, mandatory pollution check certification, covered tarpaulin for all stone trucks, and water misting.
notes: Qualitative environmental impact factor. Numerical emissions depend on fleet fuel efficiency.

material_or_source: Western DFC Rail Link (28 km electrified line)
impact_description: Electrified railway connection provides substantially lower carbon emissions per tonne-km compared to highway road transport for bulk cement and steel.
document_page: Rail DPR p18 Section 1.1; EIA p575 Table 163
evidence_text: Electric locomotive traction (103 TKM OHE electrification) ensures modal shift of bulk containerized and heavy cargo from road to rail, minimizing fossil fuel emissions.
notes: Qualitative factor. Rail has lower environmental penalty than road transport.

impact_description: Marine transport of dredged sand from Daman and precast armour units via sea avoids congestion, road wear, and community noise/dust on mainland road network.
evidence_text: Reclamation sand is extracted and delivered entirely through marine mode without utilizing terrestrial road or rail networks.
notes: Environmental advantage of marine mode over terrestrial transport for bulk sand movement.

impact_description: Statutory EMP financial budget committed by port developer for pollution control, dust suppression, water quality monitoring, and noise abatement.
evidence_text: Table 161 Budget Environmental Management Plan - Construction Phase: Total Capital Cost Rs. 302.00 Lakhs, Total Annual O&M Cost Rs. 197.35 Lakhs.
notes: Official financial allocation for environmental compliance during construction.

impact_description: Dedicated funding committed by JNPA under MoEFCC guidelines for local ecology, education, drinking water, green cover, and community welfare.
evidence_text: As per MOEFCC Office Memorandum dated 1st May 2018, JNPA has proposed an amount of Rs. 190 Crores under Corporate Environment Responsibility (CER).
notes: Statutory corporate environmental commitment for regional social and ecological development.
